claims: Legacy 1.25% convertible notes matured in 2023 and associated warrants expired by July 10, 2024; these are historical dilution, not current debt or potential-share capacity.
Current underwriting treatment therefore turns on 2026 SBC/governance, current debt balances and executed repurchases rather than the extinguished note/warrant complex.
risks: Using historical convertibles as current exposure would overstate risk; stale share counts could miss 2026 SBC/repurchase effects.
unknowns: 2026 basic/fully diluted share count, unvested awards, current debt balances and repurchase execution.
evidence.exactGate: Normalize current 2026 SBC/governance dilution, current debt and executed repurchases using the 2026 definitive proxy plus latest 2026 10-Q; exclude matured 2016 notes and expired warrants from current exposure.
evidence.nextLawfulSourcePath: Teradyne 2026 definitive proxy equity-compensation tables and latest 2026 Form 10-Q debt/equity/share-count notes.

claims: Serve reported $79.112M cash and cash equivalents at June 30, 2026 versus $106.239M at December 31, 2025 in its Q2 2026 Form 10-Q.
That cash anchor is sufficient to avoid redundant source hunting but insufficient by itself for survival/dilution/concentration treatment.
risks: Cash declined over H1; runway depends on operating cash use and financing capacity.
ATM/warrant/SBC capacity may create material dilution.
Early customer/partner concentration can amplify revenue volatility.
unknowns: Exact H1 operating cash use, unused ATM capacity, warrant/SBC overhang and current customer/partner concentration percentages.
